# spec/gates/provenance

`spec/gates/provenance` — every vector's expected value comes from
somewhere, and that holds. A `spec` source's section must state the null or
bool the vector expects. A `command` source must have printed it: until the
commands are run (`--run-sources`) the value is reported as unverified,
never as passed, and a command that failed or printed something else is a
finding. A `cite` source is the fidelity gate's.

Generated from [src/spec/gates/provenance.ts](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/src/spec/gates/provenance.ts).

## Declarations

### gateResultApart

Whether a vector cites its inputs to one section of the main RFC and its
result to another, so its result may be derived (`spec/gates/derive`).
An RFC-profile spec extracts a `spec` source only from the `; result` form
(a bare section anchor is refused there); a contract written by hand with
an RFC as its main source, a `{"spec": B}` source and a `"section": A`
takes the same rule. A module spec's `spec` rows have a main source and
never match. The report reads it too, to show both citations.

```ts
function gateResultApart(c: Contract, k: Clause): boolean
```

the contract

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="k" type="Clause" required>

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

whether k is a vector whose `spec` result is cited apart from its inputs

</scalar-field>

### gateProvenance

The provenance gate (see the module comment). It reads `ctx.sourceRuns`,
which the run-sources gate fills just before it.
